subject: Cloud dependency demarcation & SOC 2 bridge letter request - Crestfield
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestfield.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, procurement@crestfield.com
Cc: Amy Fisher <amy.fisher@kpmg.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 coverage & bridge letter for cloud dependencies

Hi Priya,

We're kicking off our vendor security review for the Crestfield integration and have a couple of items where we need Redwood's help. Specifically: 1) We need confirmation of how Redwood's hosted offering relies on cloud provider SOC reports (subservice vs shared-responsibility), and 2) whether Redwood can provide a bridge letter that extends coverage for the audit period 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30.

A few clarifying points:
- Our auditors (KPMG) need to see the mapping between your controls and the cloud provider's SOC 2 coverage (compute, storage, KMS, logging).
- Please provide your most recent list of subprocessors used for production (compute, storage, monitoring, backups).
- If a bridge letter is available, we need the exact text or an example so our auditors can confirm coverage.

Can you confirm what you can share and an estimated timeline? We have an initial audit window we want to close in early June.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of IT Risk, Crestfield Health
Attachments: crestfield-proc-checklist.xlsx (procurement checklist)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestfield.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 coverage & bridge letter for cloud dependencies

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (Security & Compliance) and Sean (Product Ops) to scope what we can deliver and by when. A few quick clarifying Qs so we can prioritize the right artifacts: 

1) Audit period: you noted 2026-07-01 -> 2027-06-30. Is that the period KPMG needs explicit bridge coverage for, or is it a rolling window where anything overlapping that period is acceptable?
2) Cloud providers: can you confirm which provider(s) you consider relevant for this review (AWS / GCP / Azure)? We need to pull provider SOCs that map to the right regions and services.
3) Controls of interest: are there specific trust services criteria your auditor is focused on (e.g., CC6: System Operations, CC7: Change Management, or specific CCs around encryption/key custody)?
4) Subprocessor depth: do you need just company-level names or the full appendix with service descriptions and contract boundaries?

What we can typically provide:
- Copy of the most recent Redwood SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where necessary) and supporting cloud provider SOC 2 reports we rely on.
- A subservice/subprocessor mapping spreadsheet that shows which responsibilities are "carve-out" vs "shared" with cloud providers.
- A draft bridge letter for your review (we often provide a templated letter that our compliance team signs).

If that works, we can target an initial package (provider SOCs + subprocessor appendix + draft bridge letter) in 4 business days once you confirm the cloud providers and acceptance criteria. If you prefer a short call to walk through the mapping, we can schedule 30 minutes early next week.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Customer Security 
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestfield.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@crestfield.com, Amy Fisher <amy.fisher@kpmg.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 coverage & bridge letter for cloud dependencies

Thanks Priya — quick answers below and attached our procurement checklist so you can see the auditor's ask.

- Audit period: 2026-07-01 -> 2027-06-30 is the period KPMG needs explicit coverage for. They will accept a bridge letter that confirms continuous coverage where the provider SOC2 covers the same controls for the stated period.
- Cloud providers: primary is AWS (us-east-1) for our production environment; we also have S3Vendor Inc for archival storage in a separate contract.
- Controls: KPMG is focused on availability (ops/change), system configuration, and encryption at rest/key management.
- Subprocessor detail: they prefer the full appendix if possible (company, service, description).

Attached: crestfield-proc-checklist.xlsx

Would appreciate the bridge letter draft and the subprocessor appendix. We can do a call Monday morning (ET).

-Liam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestfield.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 coverage & bridge letter for cloud dependencies

Hi Liam / team — Marissa here from Security & Compliance. Happy to take point. Action plan and what we'll provide: 

1) Provider artifacts: we'll attach the most recent cloud-provider SOC 2 report we rely on for compute/storage/KMS (redwood is a subservice organization for those areas) — file: cloud-provider-soc2-2026.pdf
2) Subprocessor appendix: we'll generate a CSV that lists production subprocessors, service role, and whether the function is covered by the provider SOC or managed by Redwood — file: subprocessor-appendix-2027.csv
3) Bridge letter: internal compliance will draft a bridge letter that states the coverage window and notes any carve-outs. We'll share a draft document: redwood-sample-bridge-letter-draft.docx
4) Temporary evidence: if KPMG needs interim confirmation before the full package, we can share the provider SOC and subprocessor appendix within 3 business days and the draft bridge letter in 5 business days.

Questions for KPMG (copied Amy):
- Is the provider SOC 2 (AWS) report from the same audit period sufficient, or do you need an explicit attest from the provider indicating coverage for the exact KPMG window?
- Any specific wording or disclaimers you require in the bridge letter (we typically avoid certification-like language and instead map controls to provider reports).

Next step: Priya / Sean will assemble the files and I'll circulate a draft bridge letter. Can we confirm a 30-minute call Monday 2027-05-24 10:00 AM ET? I'll send a calendar invite once confirmed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-sample-bridge-letter-draft.docx (draft bridge letter stub)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestfield.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Fisher <amy.fisher@kpmg.com>, procurement@crestfield.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 coverage & bridge letter for cloud dependencies

Marissa — that timeline works. Confirming the Monday 2027-05-24 10:00 AM ET call and that KPMG will accept the provider SOC paired with a bridge letter that maps coverage. I've added Amy to validate wording.

I'll be on the call and will bring our procurement lead. Please send the draft when ready — our auditors prefer receiving the evidence before the call if possible (even partial).

Link to calendar: https://app.docusign.com/link/ABCD1234

Talk Monday,
Liam
